title: The normalized Roos comparison respects integer shifts
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ with exact countable products [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use the unbounded derived categories of $\mathcal A$ and of its strict positive-integer inverse towers [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Let $\rho_X:\mathsf C(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim X$ be precisely the normalized Roos comparison of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison], where $\mathsf C(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod X_n\to\prod X_n)[-1]$ and $R\lim$ is computed by K-injective tower resolutions and termwise inverse limit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit, def-pur-kinjective-complex]. In coordinates $\mathsf C(X)^i=(\prod X_n)^{i-1}\oplus(\prod X_n)^i$ with differential $(y,x)\mapsto(-dy-(1-s)x,dx)$, for every $r\in\mathbf Z$ the map
$$\sigma^C_{X,r}:\mathsf C(X[r])\longrightarrow\mathsf C(X)[r],\qquad(y,x)\longmapsto((-1)^r y,x)$$
is a natural chain isomorphism. These maps give the coherent termwise Roos shift. Let $\sigma^{\lim}_{X,r}:R\lim(X[r])\to(R\lim X)[r]$ be the shift comparison represented by shifting a K-injective tower resolution $X\to I$ to $X[r]\to I[r]$ and identifying $\lim I[r]=(\lim I)[r]$. Then
$$\sigma^{\lim}_{X,r}\circ\rho_{X[r]}=\rho_X[r]\circ\sigma^C_{X,r}.$$
The normalization is retained: the inclusion $\lim I\to\mathsf C(I)$ with coordinates $(0,z)$ commutes with these shift maps. The equality is natural for all derived strict-tower morphisms, independent of the resolution and coherent for $r=0$ and addition of integers. In particular the equation applies after any natural strict-tower comparison commuting with the termwise shifts.

proof.text: Construct the natural isomorphism between the complex obtained by applying ordinary lim degreewise and the limit of the diagram of complexes: its cone has degreewise limit projections and is limiting by HomologicalComplex.isLimitOfEval. Naturality uses Mathlib IsLimit.conePointUniqueUpToIso_hom_comp directly, without restating its projection formula. The total derived-limit theorem supplies a universal pair whose unit is invertible on every K-injective. Transfer that fact to the supplied universal pair using Functor.rightDerivedNatIso and its unit equation, after the explicit ordinary-limit identification.

proof.text: For any quasi-isomorphism q:X→I with I K-injective, define d as eta_I followed by the inverse of RF(Qq), and define ds by the same construction for q[r]. Mathlib preserves quasi-isomorphisms and K-injectivity under every integer shift. Cancellation proves both normalization equations. To prove the last equation, postcompose with the isomorphism RF(Qq)[r], use naturality of cR and of the localization shift, substitute the normalization of ds, and apply the unit shift equation from step 2. The remaining expression is the shift of the normalization of d. This works for every K-injective resolution, including those without injective terms; no resolution choice is made.

lean.note: Uses the existing roosF, roosι and roosDerivedUnit constructions. The unit equation pins the supplied rho to the normalized comparison of strictRoosComparison. Coherent shifts are specified by signed chain coordinates, descent and the termwise computation for every K-injective resolution; no arbitrary shift comparison is assumed.

reviewed_lean.note: Statement matches the node clause by clause. Hypotheses are identical to strictRoosComparison (small site, universe max uC vC t, commutative ring sheaf, exact countable products, w free). _hnorm Q(roosι)≫κ≫ρ=η pins the composite κρ and is equivalent to the dependency's Q(Fq)εI⁻¹dI characterization (checked both ways). The cone shift is pinned by its x/y coordinates with r.negOnePow on y; mappingCocone.snd has sign +1 in every degree; the chain-map condition was recomputed in Lean sign conventions. The descended shift is pinned through κ; the derived-limit shift is pinned both by ρ-conjugation and by the every-K-injective-resolution clause (d and ds unique), so the main square is not a tautology. The limit shift is the identity on compatible tuples. The (0,z) inclusion clause and the CommShift coherence for r=0 and addition are present. The only stmt_deps change adds the landed def-weil-strict-roos-model, whose declarations appear in the signature. lean.statement is verbatim, there is one sorry, and the docstrings carry the Stacks places and blueprint id. Not a duplicate of RoosCommShift (strict level, different functor). Advisory: two plain imports are redundant. No compile run, per instruction; no files changed.
